"The Doll" is a 1938 British romantic comedy film directed by Ernest Morris. The film stars Ben Field, G.H. Mulcaster, Esma Cannon, and Dennis Arundell.

The story follows a wealthy doll manufacturer named John Hewitt who falls in love with his niece's governess, Mary. To win her over, he poses as a common laborer in order to see if she loves him for who he is, rather than his money.

The film is based on the 1927 play "The Doll" by Ferenc Molnár, which was also adapted into a 1929 film of the same name. The plot centers around mistaken identities, misunderstandings, and comedic situations.

"The Doll" received positive reviews for its charming and humorous storyline, as well as the performances of the cast. It is considered a classic British romantic comedy from the 1930s.

Overall, "The Doll" is a light-hearted and entertaining film that showcases the talents of its actors and director in bringing a beloved stage play to the big screen.
